The upsampled decoder features are concatenated with corresponding high resolution encoder feature maps for better localization. DeconvNet [11] encoder consists of convolutional layers and two fully connected layers of VGG16. Andersen 1 Abstract— The development of autonomous agricultural ve- hicles depends on accurate visual interpretation of the envi- ronment. Semantic pixel-wise segmentation plays an important role in achieving a more detailed description of the scene and understanding of the spatial-relationship between different objects. In this paper, a deep architecture for road scene and indoor scene segmentation, SegNet, is applied in solving the scene recognition problem for the agricultural environment. The network is trained on an agriculture image dataset collected during ﬁeld operation. The problem focuses on the segmentation of ﬁve classes of structures commonly found in the ﬁelds: vegetation, grass, ground, crop ﬁeld and obstacles. We apply frequency balancing to address the challenge of class imbalance and transfer learning technique. The quantitative performance of the network is evaluated using pixel accuracy and intersec- tion over union metrics. Moreover, we present an approach for an inﬁeld qualitative validation of the trained network. I. I NTRODUCTION According to the latest UN World Population Prospects, the world’s population is projected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050 and 10.9 billion by 2100 [1]. In order to meet the increasing food demands and provide sustainable agricultural growth, it is essential to implement the more efﬁcient use of land, labour and other inputs through technological progress, social innovation and new business models [2]. The future vision of sustainable agricultural growth re- lies on technological innovation in the areas of precision agriculture, robotic systems and information technologies [3]. The recent availability of large-scale datasets, use of GPU computing, and increased computing power led to the application of AI technologies in a wide range of businesses and industries. The goal of semantic segmentation is to annotate each pixel within an image with a semantically interpretable class from a predeﬁned set of classes. This annotation helps achieve a detailed description of the object boundaries and better understanding of the spatial relationship between different structures present in the scene. This research work aims to advance the real-life appli- cation of semantic segmentation in scene perception for the agricultural environment. The SegNet encoder-decoder architecture [8] is applied in solving the segmentation task. This architecture was selected due to its practical advantages. Compared to architectures presented in [9] and [10], SegNet provides a memory-efﬁcient storing of information from encoder feature maps by using only max-pooling indices. The work presented in [11] uses a similar technique for upsampling in the decoder network, but it has a signiﬁcantly larger number of parameters. Moreover, SegNet is a fully convolutional network and can therefore take input images of arbitrary size. To the best of our knowledge, SegNet architecture has not been applied before in solving scene segmentation task for agricultural vehicles. The main barrier in transferring semantic pixel-wise seg- mentation architectures to agriculture is limited availability of labelled datasets [12]. Therefore, an important contribu- tion of our work is training and performance evaluation of the segmentation network on a new image dataset collected speciﬁcally for the agricultural domain. The images were collected during tractor’s operation in the crop ﬁeld and represent a realistic scenario for driving in the agricultural environment. The dataset contains ﬁve labelled classes of ﬁeld structures: “Vegetation”, “Grass”, “Ground”, “Crop ﬁeld”, and “Obstacle”. Moreover, we present an approach for continuous quali- tative validation of the network in practice. Towards Semantic Scene Segmentation for Autonomous Agricultural Vehicles Esma Mujkic 1,2, Dan Hermann 2, Ole Ravn 1, Morten L. Bilde 2 and Nils A. Andersen 1 Abstract— The development of autonomous agricultural ve- hicles depends on accurate visual interpretation of the envi- ronment. Semantic pixel-wise segmentation plays an important role in achieving a more detailed description of the scene and understanding of the spatial-relationship between different objects. In this paper, a deep architecture for road scene and indoor scene segmentation, SegNet, is applied in solving the scene recognition problem for the agricultural environment. The network is trained on an agriculture image dataset collected during ﬁeld operation. The problem focuses on the segmentation of ﬁve classes of structures commonly found in the ﬁelds: vegetation, grass, ground, crop ﬁeld and obstacles. We apply frequency balancing to address the challenge of class imbalance and transfer learning technique. The quantitative performance of the network is evaluated using pixel accuracy and intersec- tion over union metrics. Moreover, we present an approach for an inﬁeld qualitative validation of the trained network. I. The goal of semantic segmentation is to annotate each pixel within an image with a semantically interpretable class from a predeﬁned set of classes. This annotation helps achieve a detailed description of the object boundaries and better understanding of the spatial relationship between different structures present in the scene. This research work aims to advance the real-life appli- cation of semantic segmentation in scene perception for the agricultural environment. The SegNet encoder-decoder architecture [8] is applied in solving the segmentation task. This architecture was selected due to its practical advantages. Compared to architectures presented in [9] and [10], SegNet provides a memory-efﬁcient storing of information from encoder feature maps by using only max-pooling indices. The work presented in [11] uses a similar technique for upsampling in the decoder network, but it has a signiﬁcantly larger number of parameters. Moreover, SegNet is a fully convolutional network and can therefore take input images of arbitrary size. To the best of our knowledge, SegNet architecture has not been applied before in solving scene segmentation task for agricultural vehicles. The main barrier in transferring semantic pixel-wise seg- mentation architectures to agriculture is limited availability of labelled datasets [12]. Therefore, an important contribu- tion of our work is training and performance evaluation of the segmentation network on a new image dataset collected speciﬁcally for the agricultural domain. The images were collected during tractor’s operation in the crop ﬁeld and represent a realistic scenario for driving in the agricultural environment. The dataset contains ﬁve labelled classes of ﬁeld structures: “Vegetation”, “Grass”, “Ground”, “Crop ﬁeld”, and “Obstacle”. Moreover, we present an approach for continuous quali- tative validation of the network in practice.
